title: Make all PDF output paths atomic and rollback-safe
description: merge_pdfs, split_pdf, rotate_pdf_pages, reorder_pdf_pages, apply_page_plan, and some bulk paths write directly to final destinations. A write or multi-output failure can truncate an existing output, leave partial files, or advance lifecycle state inconsistently.
design: Route single-output PDF mutations through the canonical same-directory temporary write plus rename path with explicit durability and overwrite policy. Give multi-output split and bulk operations a transaction-like staging and commit contract with rollback or a complete partial-result report. Add injected failures for write, rename, permission, disk-full simulation, and mid-batch errors.
acceptance_criteria: Every PDF-producing handler has a declared atomicity and overwrite policy; injected failures preserve pre-existing output bytes and source bytes; no temporary residue remains; active-document state advances only after successful commit; split and bulk failures either commit the entire declared set or return an exact retained partial set without misreporting success; focused and full regression suites pass.
notes:
2026-07-21 same-document commits now use fsynced same-directory temp files, atomic rename, durable pending/committed journal, per-document interprocess locks, and final optimistic recheck. This materially hardens the path but does not close this bead: merge, split, rotate, reorder, page-plan, and multi-output rollback policies still need the full acceptance matrix.

title: Preserve original backup identity across deletion and restart
description: Same-path mutation backup identity currently depends on the in-process backupPathByCanonical map. If the remembered backup disappears, ensureBackupForCanonicalPath recreates a new backup from the current possibly mutated PDF and can present it as the original. Restart also loses the mapping.
design: Persist and verify immutable original identity for each canonical document, including original SHA-256 and backup SHA-256. A missing or mismatched original backup must fail closed with an actionable recovery path rather than copying current mutated bytes. Cover H0 to H1 to H2, backup deletion, restart or rehydration, and concurrent access.
acceptance_criteria: The first same-path mutation creates one backup equal to H0; later mutations keep the same path and H0 hash; deleting or tampering with that backup never creates a replacement from H1 or H2 labeled as original; restart or rehydration preserves or safely refuses the relationship; failures do not advance active-document state; tests include exact hashes and independent reopen.
notes: 2026-07-21 fixed in a0e9ba5 and verified at 10d11e0. Durable per-canonical-path H0 record binds backup path, original SHA-256, last committed SHA-256, and pending journal state. Missing/tampered backup, deleted record, legacy evidence, forged rehydration, file/directory symlinks, restart, external replacement, and concurrent mutation all fail closed or preserve one H0 as contracted. The missing-backup campaign passes 3/3. Acceptance met across focused and repeated fidelity evidence.

title: Build detect_signature_zones helper + tool
description: Agents currently stamp signatures at arbitrary coordinates because they have no way to locate the actual sign-here spot (proven: W-9 test put signature on General Instructions, not the signature line). New tool returns a typed-zone list so agents never guess coordinates again.
design: Layered detection in helpers.js: (1) AcroForm signature-typed fields -> confidence 0.99 via form.getFields filter; (2) AcroForm text fields named like /sig|initial/i -> 0.85; (3) pdfjs text extraction with bounding boxes -> scan for 'Signature of', 'Sign Here', 'Initial', 'Date:' patterns -> 0.70-0.90 per pattern; (4) adjacent rectangle detection for initials boxes -> 0.75. Returns array of { type, label, page, x, y, width, height, confidence, source } with top-left origin coords. New tool detect_signature_zones wired in server/index.js.

title: Fix redirect-based SSRF in fetch_pdf_from_url

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] downloadPdfFromUrl follows redirects manually

- [ ] All existing fetch tests still pass
close_reason: Manual redirect following with per-hop isPrivateHost validation. Added 7 tests covering: reject redirect to 169.254.169.254, reject redirect to localhost, reject redirect to RFC1918, allow public-to-public redirect, reject redirect loops > maxRedirects, resolve relative Location headers, never write a file on rejected redirect. title: Recover interrupted multi-output PDF transactions
description: Split and bulk PDF commits now stage the complete set and roll back handler-observed failures, but an abrupt process or host termination during the activation window can leave stage/rollback artifacts or a partially activated set. Add a durable, integrity-bound transaction journal and startup or pre-commit recovery that deterministically restores or completes interrupted transactions without trusting forged paths.
acceptance_criteria: Kill-process fault injection at every activation boundary proves deterministic recovery; journal paths are allowlisted, canonical, regular-file-only, and integrity-bound; pre-existing bytes are restored or the complete new set is finished; recovery is idempotent; no transaction artifacts remain after recovery; Linux and packed-host regression evidence passes.
notes: Selected immediately after igr.15. Implement a versioned same-directory journal with integrity digest, strict regular-file/path validation, deterministic rollback for prepared/activating state, committed-state cleanup, idempotent recovery, and kill-point tests. Keep public claims bounded to tested process-death points and current single-directory split/bulk behavior.

title: Stop page analysis from classifying extraction failures as blank

design: Track per-page analysis provenance and failure explicitly. A page with failed or incomplete analysis must be unknown, never likely blank. Require successful text/image/content measurements before blank classification and surface retry guidance.
acceptance_criteria: Forced PDF.js whole-document and per-page failures produce unknown/degraded results with no likely-blank claim; successful blank/nonblank fixtures retain expected classifications; apply_page_plan workflows cannot interpret unknown as deletion advice; source/share and packed contract tests pass.

title: Make save-lifecycle tests order-independent
description: Fixed-seed shuffled execution exposes shared-state contamination in test/save-lifecycle.test.js. Two lifecycle tests pass only because declared order leaves the shared TMP_DIR in the expected state; when the rotation case runs first, its PDFs pollute later top-level file assertions. This is identical under Vitest 4.1.4 and 4.1.10, so it is a pre-existing suite defect rather than an upgrade regression.

Keep assertions explicit about allowed, created, backed-up, and unrelated files. Add a stable shuffled-seed command to CI or a focused order-permutation regression without making the suite nondeterministically flaky.

title: Make validate_pdf report field completeness truthfully
description: A real headless agent fill trial exposed misleading completeness semantics: validate_pdf reports every unchecked checkbox as filled and infers requiredness only from field-name substrings. The W-9 fixture had multiple false checkbox values, yet the report claimed 21 of 22 fields filled. This can give an agent or user false confidence that a form is complete.
design: Define field-type-aware statuses (text nonempty, checkbox checked/unchecked/not-applicable, radio/dropdown selection) without equating unchecked with filled. Separate observed value coverage from required-field completeness. Use actual PDF required flags when available; label heuristics explicitly and never claim whole-form validity from them. Return structuredContent with counts, per-field status, limitations, and a stable schema while retaining a readable text fallback.
acceptance_criteria: W-9 and synthetic fixtures prove unchecked boxes are not counted as filled; true PDF required flags are honored where supported; text/dropdown/radio/checkbox semantics have regression tests; structured output distinguishes observed, empty, unchecked, required-missing, unknown, and read-error states; report explicitly states when completeness cannot be determined; real agent fill-and-validate trajectory cannot pass solely from an inflated filled count.
notes:
Discovered 2026-07-21 by real Codex MCP trial. Output SHA-256 8e7a2c45d5896bf697161cb18aeb47703e2198f71f8e0eaccbf16cffdf33a617; validate_pdf reported 22 total / 21 filled / 1 empty despite multiple false checkboxes. Independent read_pdf_fields confirmed the five requested values were correct, so artifact correctness and form-completeness claims must remain separate.

title: Fix detached ArrayBuffer on working-copy reload
description: Viewer reload after stamping to the same -signed.pdf working-copy path can reuse stale cached byte ranges keyed only by path+offset. Fix by invalidating cached range entries/inflight requests for the stamped path before reloading the overwritten working copy; add regression coverage around cache eviction behavior.
close_reason: Implemented and pushed in commit 45ba16b; viewer now invalidates per-path byte-range cache epochs before reloading an overwritten working copy, preventing stale chunk reuse and detached ArrayBuffer errors on same-path -signed.pdf refreshes.

title: Vite dev mode for the viewer — mocked ext-apps SDK + MCP bridge
description: Iterating on the viewer UI currently requires: edit code -> npm run build:ui -> mcpb pack -> open .mcpb -> Mat clicks Install -> Mat Cmd+Q and relaunches Claude Desktop -> Mat reproduces bug -> Mat screenshots -> back to me. 5-10 min per cycle. Unworkable for UX polish. \n\nClaude Desktop hardens against CDP automation (codesign entitlements show no disable-library-validation / get-task-allow), so we can't drive the desktop app remotely. But the viewer is a self-contained single-file HTML + TS app — it CAN run in Chrome if we mock the @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps SDK and route app.callServerTool to a local MCP server subprocess. That drops the iteration loop to ~20 seconds and lets an agent use /browse or gstack to drive the viewer directly.
design:
Three files + vite.config + package.json additions.

1) ui/dev/mock-ext-apps.ts — shims the @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps module. Exports App class, McpUiHostContext type, applyDocumentTheme / applyHostStyleVariables noops. App implements: connect() (fires fake host-context event), getHostContext() (returns { tool_input: { pdf_path, display_mode } } from URL query params so you can ?pdf_path=example-fw9.pdf), callServerTool({name,arguments}) (POSTs to /__dev__/tool), sendSizeChanged/updateModelContext/requestDisplayMode (mostly noops that resolve trivially), on(event, fn) (event listener mock).

2) ui/dev/bridge-plugin.mjs — Vite plugin. configureServer hook: spawn  as a child process on startup, attach a simple JSON-RPC correlator over its stdin/stdout (MCP protocol — initialize, initialized, tools/call). Middleware for POST /__dev__/tool that takes {name,arguments}, sends tools/call JSON-RPC to the child, awaits response keyed by rpc id, returns JSON { content, structuredContent, isError }. On server shutdown, kill the child process cleanly.

3) vite.config.mjs — import bridge-plugin.mjs, conditionally add it only when mode==='development'. Add resolve.alias entry to point '@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps' at ui/dev/mock-ext-apps.ts when in dev mode. Keep production build completely untouched — viteSingleFile still produces dist-ui/index.html for mcpb.

4) package.json scripts:  -> . Maybe also  that clears .test-tmp-golden/ and ~/.pdf-toolkit-files/signatures/quick-* so test state resets.

5) ui/dev/index.html (optional) — dev-specific entry if we need to inject ?pdf_path=... defaults. Alternatively just use the existing ui/index.html and read location.search.

When an agent runs , Vite starts at localhost:5173, the MCP server spawns as child of vite, the viewer loads with a default PDF, and every app.callServerTool call round-trips to the real server. Agent drives the viewer via gstack or /browse, captures screenshots, iterates on TS/CSS with instant HMR. No MCPB pack cycle.

description: Two concurrent fetch_pdf_from_url calls with the same URL both resolve to 'foo.pdf', both write to the same file. Low frequency in real usage but real race.
design: Switch writeFile to exclusive flag 'wx'. On EEXIST, rerun findUniquePath and retry, up to 5 times. Alternative: use a per-user mutex keyed on target path.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] writeFile uses 'wx' flag\n- [ ] Retry loop handles EEXIST\n- [ ] Test with Promise.all of 10 concurrent fetches of same URL — no collisions, no crashes
